newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- Pilots at American Airlines, which is owned by AMR Corp, voted down the tentative contract agreement that their union's leaders had reached with the company in September.
- Texaco Inc dismissed one senior executive, suspended another and cut off benefits to two retirees for engaging in improper conduct that was secretly recorded.
- Economists are more optimistic about the economy's vigour, and talk in many quarters has turned to how long the inflation-wary Fed can wait before tightening policy.
- Pillsbury Inc, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, has taken just a few years to become the world's biggest maker of Mexican food.
- Stocks dropped sharply late in the session.
- Entergy AKP_p.N is moving aggressively into the business of running nuclear plants for other electrical companies.
- The first trickle of software for digital video disks was released.
- Grayhound plans to start a bus route between Los Angeles and Ciudad Obregon, Mexico.
- IBM plans to announce it will make more than two million patent filings available free on the World Wide Web.
- General Motors said it expected to reverse the long decline in the company's share of the American market.
- The Labour Department has enlisted state officials in a programme to protect consumers who are denied health benefits by self-insured companies.
- Fifty-three people were charged in a case in which they allegedly paid stand-ins to take exams for a stockbrokers licence.
- New rules for the Nasdaq stock market that are aimed at giving investors better prices when they buy and sell were delayed until January 20.
- Millions of retirees are nearly as well off as they were in their working years, but they are absorbing even more Social Security and Medicare dollars.
